summary: Re-deliver an order's tickets — the write that does not exist yet
description:
Carved out of **TKT-194** when its scope survey found there is nothing to call.

**No resend exists anywhere.** Delivery is a side effect of consuming the issuance event
(`services/access/internal/consumer/consumer.go:410-423`): access reads the buyer's address from
commerce's `/internal/buyers/{id}/delivery-email`, sends the guest link, and calls `MarkDelivered`.
There is no endpoint, in any service, that re-triggers it — and the ticket query filters on
`NOT EXISTS (… event_type='delivered')`, so simply replaying the event would deliver nothing.

So a resend is a **new write**, not a UI for an existing one, and it is the more interesting half to
design:

- It sends **PII-bearing mail** on staff command, which is a different act from sending it as the
  automatic consequence of a purchase. Who may trigger it, how often, and to which address are all
  decisions the issuance path never had to make.
- **The address is the whole question.** Sending to the address on file is safe and often useless —
  the customer is calling *because* they cannot receive it. Sending to an address the staff member
  types turns the back office into a mail relay that emits ticket capabilities to arbitrary
  recipients, which is a fraud surface, not a feature.
- A resend re-emits a **guest retrieval capability** (ADR-012). Every send widens the set of people
  holding it, and nothing revokes the old one.
- It needs its own lifecycle event, or the trail says the ticket was delivered once when it was
  delivered four times (ADR-021: the trail's claim must match what happened).

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] A staff member can re-deliver a completed order's tickets, and the trail records **each**
      delivery, not just the first.
- [ ] The destination address is decided explicitly: on-file only, or operator-supplied with a
      stated control. **Name the fraud case you are refusing** — an operator-supplied address is how
      tickets get mailed to someone who did not buy them.
- [ ] Rate-limited or bounded per order, with the bound written down rather than implied.
- [ ] The back office does not gain the ability to *read* the buyer's address as a side effect
      (ADR-042 keeps it credential-less for commerce's internal surface; TKT-201 owns that read).
- [ ] Idempotency: a double-click sends one mail.
- [ ] `make check` green.

**Worth settling at shaping:** whether resend belongs to the back office at all, or to a
self-service "resend my tickets" flow on the storefront keyed by something the buyer knows. The
second needs no staff credential and no fraud surface, and answers the same customer problem.

governingAdrs.why: A resend re-emits the guest retrieval capability. Every send widens who holds it, and nothing revokes the previous one.
The buyer's address is PII. Where it is read, and whether it is ever written to a trail, is this ticket's decision to make explicitly.
If the trail says 'delivered' once for four deliveries, the trail is making a claim that is not true. Each send is its own event.
The back office holds no commerce credential by design — a resend must not become the back door to the buyer-contact read.

reference.summary: Delivery as it exists: a side effect of the issuance consumer, with no way to re-trigger it.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Filed from TKT-194's scope survey (2026-08-04). Same shape as TKT-201: the ticket assumed a write that does not exist. Not shaped — needs the 8-item DoR before Gate 1.

The open question in the description is the real one: a storefront self-service resend may answer the same customer problem with no staff credential and no fraud surface.
